name: Familial Bicuspid Aortic Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Bicuspid Aortic Valve

criteria.description: Echocardiographic visualization of aortic valve with two cusps instead of three
Positive family history of bicuspid aortic valve or related aortopathy
Presence of aortic root or ascending aorta dilation on imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of bicuspid aortic valve morphology; family history supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely required

rare.symptomName: Abnormal left ventricular outflow tract morphology

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Blood cultures positive in infective endocarditis
imaging: Echocardiography showing bicuspid aortic valve morphology
CT or MRI demonstrating ascending aortic dilation or aneurysm
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly or aortic contour abnormalities
other: Electrocardiogram showing left ventricular hypertrophy in stenosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of three aortic valve cusps on echocardiography
Lower risk of aortic dilation compared to bicuspid valve
Aortic root dilation with tricuspid valve morphology

redFlags: Rapid progression of aortic stenosis symptoms
Sudden onset chest pain suggestive of aortic dissection
Signs of heart failure or syncope
references: Michelena HI, et al. Bicuspid Aortic Valve: Identifying Knowledge Gaps and Rising to the Challenge From the International Bicuspid Aortic Valve Consortium (BAVCon). Circulation. 2014.
Fedak PWM, et al. Clinical and Pathophysiological Implications of Bicuspid Aortic Valve. Circulation. 2002.
